title: Career mosaic — manager briefing notes
content:
Purpose of this note:
- Short, handheld packet to bring to my next 1:1 with Priya (manager) — focused, evidence-backed, and with clear asks.
- Treat as scratch: leave rough fragments, examples, TODOs here and refine before share.

Top-line ask (one sentence):
- I want to discuss a path to Senior People Partner within 12 months, identify two sponsorship opportunities, and agree on stretch deliverables that will be visible to GTM and Eng leadership.

Context / why now:
- Last promotion cycle I was scoped as IC-2; feedback highlighted cross-functional influence and project delivery as areas to grow.
- Over the past 9 months I led onboarding redesign (project ORCHID) that cut time-to-ramp by ~18% for hires in product roles.
- Current hiring mix and growth plans (Q2 hiring surge) create window to own a cross-org initiative that demonstrates scale impact.

Impact evidence (concise bullets I can say out loud):
- ORCHID onboarding: owned scope, stakeholder alignment, launch plan. Measuring: baseline time-to-first-PR 32d -> 26d (rolling 90d cohort). Linked: HR-412.
- Interview experience revamp: introduced standardized scorecard for PM interviews; adoption across three interview loops. Early signal: downstream offer acceptance for PMs increased by 4 percentage points in pilot teams.
- Manager coaching: ran 6 micro-cohorts for first-time managers, NPS avg 78.

Examples / short stories to use in conversation:
- "When engineering leads flagged inconsistent ramp outcomes, I convened product+eng hiring managers and built a 'first-12-weeks' playbook. I negotiated scope reductions to ship within 6 weeks and measured the outcome with hiring managers weekly."
- "I prioritized blunt, tiny experiments — e.g., 2-week buddy pairing trial — which we could measure quickly. That experiment alone improved new-hire PR cadence and gave managers confidence to adjust interview calibration."

Skills to highlight (evidence-based):
- Cross-functional persuasion: got 5 hiring managers to commit to new intake templating in one meeting.
- Data-informed ops: built a small funnel dashboard (sheet + scripts) to track ramp metrics and surfaced it in weekly hiring syncs.
- Program execution: shipped ORCHID MVP across 4 teams on time.

Gaps and development plan (what I want help with):
- Bigger-project visibility: need sponsorship to get 1 executive-level stakeholder attached to a program so outcomes are visible in leadership rituals.
- Strategic breadth: want to be looped into quarterly workforce planning earlier — shadow Priya in planning cycle?
- Influence at scale: practice narrative design for exec audiences; ask for feedback on two upcoming cross-functional okr reviews.

Concrete asks for this 1:1 (pick 2–3):
1) Sponsor intro: Can you introduce me to either Manu (Head of Engineering) or Clara (VP GTM) to propose a cross-org strategic onboarding program that covers Eng + GTM hires?
2) Stretch assignment: Give me lead for Q2 hiring calibration playbook and priority to present at next monthly People & Growth sync.
3) Feedback loop: Block 30 minutes post-Q2 planning for a dry-run of the executive narrative — can you attend and give live feedback?
4) Compensation calibration: If we agree on expanded scope, can you outline timeline for promotion packet and what evidence you need?

Signals of success (shared metrics):
- Reduced median time-to-first-PR for product and eng hires by 20% within 6 months of program start.
- Adoption of onboarding playbook by 60% of hiring managers in targeted orgs.
- At least one exec meeting where I present program outcomes and secure a second-phase budget request.

Potential objections I should be ready for and short counters:
- "We don't have bandwidth" -> "I intend to own execution, and I will propose a trimmed MVP to limit lift; initial impact can be measured in 6–8 weeks."
- "This overlaps with existing L&D work" -> "I propose a cross-functional working group with clear ownership boundaries; this would complement L&D by focusing on role-specific ramp, not generic training."

Calibration notes (what I need from manager in this meeting):
- Explicit guidance on what counts as "senior" in our framework (examples of visible outcomes).
- Clear timeline for promotion packet and who needs to be involved.
- Sponsor names and likely objections to expect from them.

Preparation checklist (before 1:1):
- Pull the ORCHID cohort dashboard + 2-slide snapshot (impact + plan) — DONE (sheet id in linked_artifacts).
- Draft 3-paragraph exec narrative + 1 slide mockup — draft v0 in this doc.
- Identify potential MVP scope and resource estimate (hours/week, likely collaborators) — TODO: add estimates.
- Create short candidate list for sponsors (Manu, Clara, Juliette).

Open questions I want to ask manager (short list):
- Which one of my recent projects would you cite as the clearest evidence of readiness?
- What is the most convincing format for a promotion packet in our org (doc vs presentation vs checklist)?
- Who typically advocates for people-ops promotions at SLT reviews?

Notes to self (scratch/fragments):
- Keep examples quant + short — avoid long process descriptions.
- Prepare a one-liner for Slack announcement if we get approval (so it looks polished).
- Consider gathering 2 manager quotes (quick Slack DM) to include in packet.

Post-meeting follow-ups (placeholders):
- Email sponsor intros with 1-paragraph ask and an attached 2-slide summary.
- Update promotion packet checklist and set internal review date.
- Book rehearsal with Priya for exec narrative.

Small wins log (to add to packet):
- ORCHID: 18% faster ramp (Q4->Q1 comparison).
- Micro-cohort manager training: NPS 78.
- Interview scorecards rolled to 3 loops.

Final quick draft pitch (1 minute):
"I want to move from a program-focused IC to a role where I lead cross-functional initiatives that demonstrably shift ramp and retention for product and engineering hires. I have evidence from our ORCHID pilot, and a concrete MVP that can be executed in 6–8 weeks if we attach a sponsor and give me visibility into Q2 planning. My ask today is for two things: your sponsorship for presenting to Manu or Clara, and the lead seat on the calibration playbook so we can show measurable outcomes by mid-Q3."

Version history / edits notes:
- 2025-02-03 initial sketch
- 2025-02-24 added ORCHID metrics + micro-cohort NPS
- 2025-03-11 refined asks and added sponsor list

TODO (short):

- [ ] DM two hiring managers for short quotes
- [ ] Draft sponsor outreach email template

End of note.
